scientific_question: Can one pooled cost-aware ML state policy directly select and hold the highest expected after-cost position among Bybit BTCUSDT, ETHUSDT, SOLUSDT and XRPUSDT strongly enough to beat the current 0.07001887213879954% geometric-daily first place at the same 24-bp comparison cost without a named setup library?
economic_mechanism: At each completed hour the model estimates the next executable-hour directional delivery for all four contracts. The account compares every long, short and flat action with its current one-slot position after explicit turnover and funding costs. It changes state only when another action has higher positive net utility; otherwise the position persists. Already-completed rolling 24-hour opposite liquidity is the emergency invalidation and trails only toward price.
trader_translation: The completed 24-hour high and low are the nearest higher-timeframe external liquidity and invalidation references.
Continuous displacement, path efficiency, volatility, volume and cross-asset breadth describe whether current delivery is likely to continue.
ML ranks the four markets and both directions by expected net delivery after the cost of leaving the current position.
The one global slot is assigned only to the highest positive expected utility; no setup name or second model can authorize a trade.
A position is not liquidated because an hour elapsed. It remains open until the cost-aware policy changes or the causal structural stop is reached.

source.provider: Bybit public historical data and public V5 market API
source.availability: A source bar is usable only after its full UTC hour is complete; entry uses the following hourly open.
source.funding_fallback: When complete historical funding cannot be retrieved, every crossed UTC 00/08/16 settlement is charged an adverse 2bp reserve rather than omitted.

model.calibration: One non-negative zero-intercept least-squares scale fitted only on the calibration partition and clipped to [0,2].
model.target: log of the following executable hourly open divided by the entry hourly open
model.direction_and_symbol: The one model score is evaluated for long and short on every symbol; no separate direction model exists.

policy.actions: FLAT plus LONG or SHORT on exactly one of the four symbols
policy.turnover_cost: Half of the frozen round-trip cost for each exited or entered unit of notional; a reversal or symbol switch pays both sides.
policy.decision_utility: predicted directional account return minus 2 times immediate turnover cost minus a 2bp adverse settlement reserve when applicable
policy.structural_stop: already-known rolling 24-hour opposite extreme; after entry it can trail only toward the position
policy.source_boundary: Any open position receives the full remaining structural-stop loss and exit cost.
policy.same_hour_rule: Only the structural stop is intrahour; if crossed, the stop is applied before the next hourly mark.
policy.top_trade_counterfactual: Remove the largest positive 10% completed episode start keys and rerun the full state and one-slot path.

chronology.opening_rule: Development is read only after every confirmation gate passes. Official 2024-2026 data are not accessed in this fatal screen.

conditional_risk_and_leverage_search.opening: Only after the complete confirmation gate passes.
conditional_risk_and_leverage_search.quantity: risk fraction divided by entry-to-structural-stop distance, capped by the tested notional multiple
conditional_risk_and_leverage_search.selection: highest confirmation geometric daily growth among paths with positive ordinary and winner-removed return, at least 50 trades, no ruin and MDD below 80%
conditional_risk_and_leverage_search.reason: Risk and leverage are not restricted before evidence; they are explored widely only after the frozen information unit has robust positive after-cost expectancy.

authority.next_if_survivor: Freeze the selected model, calibrator, policy and risk rule, then replay causal half-year Bybit account paths from 2024 through 2026 with exact BBO/depth, actual funding, latency, capacity and liquidation-distance stress.
